title: Junior Science and Humanities Symposium (JSHS)
organization: Army Educational Outreach Program (AEOP) / U.S. Department of War
description: National STEM research symposium for U.S. high school students in grades 9-12. Students conduct original STEM research and present/compete for scholarships at one of 49 regional symposia; top performers advance to the National JSHS. Over $400,000 in scholarships and awards available across the program.
residency_restrictions: Open to students in U.S. states/territories and DoDEA (Department of Defense Education Activity) schools overseas, per program description -- not confirmed open to students outside the U.S. school system.
current_cycle_label: Program was recently reinstated after a suspension; the official site (jshs.org) was itself mid-update at time of research, with 2026/2027 cycle deadlines not yet posted ("more details are on the way").
verification_status: Verified - official government-program page (usaeop.com, the Army Educational Outreach Program) fetched and read; jshs.org itself could not be directly fetched by the research tool (a domain-safety check, not a content block), but the AEOP page explicitly and directly confirms JSHS's current status, eligibility, and structure
research_notes: An earlier WebSearch pass surfaced a stale claim that JSHS was 'suspended until further notice' -- the actual current official page (fetched directly) says JSHS 'has officially returned', confirming the earlier search snippet was outdated. This is a live example of why a fetched page must always override a search snippet. No cost figure was confirmed on the page actually fetched (a separate, unverified search result described it as free) -- left null rather than assert a figure I didn't personally confirm.

title: Hack Club
description: Global nonprofit membership community for teenage makers: 1,500+ in-person high-school clubs worldwide plus an online community, running a rotating slate of free build challenges/events, and financial and technical tools for teen-led tech projects. Not a single event -- an ongoing community students can join at any time.
application_requirements: join online community or start/join a local club
current_cycle_label: Ongoing membership community, not cycle-bound -- join at any time.
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read
research_notes: Umbrella organization -- see companion record NIGHT1-SELF-03 (Hack Club: Stardance) for one of its current specific dated build-challenge programs. Official site states it is free 'for every teenager, forever'. HQ is Burlington, Vermont (US) but the club network and online community are explicitly global.

title: Hack Club: Stardance
organization: Hack Club, in partnership with NASA, AMD, and GitHub
description: Free STEM summer build event run by Hack Club in partnership with NASA, AMD, and GitHub -- one of Hack Club's rotating dated build-challenge programs, open to teen makers.
current_cycle_label: Runs through September 30, 2026 -- still open to join as of this research date (2026-08-21).
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read
research_notes: Specific program mechanics (exact deliverable, judging if any) were not fully confirmed beyond the homepage summary -- description kept intentionally general rather than guessing specifics. This is a time-boxed program ending 2026-09-30, so it will need refreshing or retiring shortly after that date -- flag for the freshness-cadence system rather than treating as evergreen like NIGHT1-SELF-02.

title: Jane Goodall's Roots & Shoots (USA)
description: Free youth environmental and humanitarian action movement founded by Jane Goodall. Members (individuals, classrooms, or community groups) design and run their own community-led service projects using a '4-Step Formula' (Get Inspired, Observe, Take Action, Celebrate). US chapter reports 2,118 registered groups across all 50 states; sister chapters exist in Canada, the UK, and globally (see research_notes) but were not independently verified this pass.
application_requirements: online registration as an individual or group
current_cycle_label: Ongoing movement, not cycle-bound -- register and start a project at any time.
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read
research_notes: No explicit minimum/maximum age was stated on the page fetched -- left null rather than guess, though the program is clearly youth/school-group oriented (a Youth Council USA exists per search results). This record covers the US chapter specifically (rootsandshoots.org); separate chapter sites exist for Canada (janegoodall.ca), the UK (rootsnshoots.org.uk), and a Global hub (janegoodall.global/roots-shoots/) -- worth a follow-up pass to confirm whether non-US students can register directly via the US site or must use a country-specific chapter, and to add those chapters as their own records if materially different. A second candidate, Ashoka Young Changemakers (a global youth social-entrepreneurship fellowship, ages under 20, active in US/Nigeria/Brazil/India/Bangladesh/Indonesia per WebSearch), was investigated but dropped from this batch: ashoka.org returned HTTP 403 on two separate fetch attempts, so it could not be page-verified and is left as an unverified lead for a future pass rather than published on search-only evidence.

title: Congress-Bundestag Youth Exchange (CBYX) for High School Students
organization: U.S. Department of State, in partnership with the German Bundestag
description: Government-sponsored merit-based youth exchange sending U.S. high school students to Germany for a full academic year of study and cultural immersion, administered by the U.S. Department of State together with the German Bundestag. No prior German language skills required.
citizenship_restrictions: U.S. citizens only, per the official page fetched.
selectivity_evidence: Official State Department page describes it as providing 'merit-based scholarships' with a minimum GPA floor of 2.5, implying a competitive review beyond the GPA gate, though no numeric acceptance rate was published.
current_cycle_label: A search result (not independently page-verified this pass) referenced a 2026-27 CBYX High School Application page at usagermanyscholarship.org -- not confirmed directly; check that site for exact current deadlines before displaying one to students.
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read
research_notes: Widely known publicly to be a fully-funded U.S. State Department exchange (travel, tuition, homestay covered), but the specific official page fetched this pass did not itself state a cost figure or confirm fully-funded status in as many words -- left cost/financial_aid_available null rather than assert from outside knowledge not directly confirmed on the fetched page. A companion candidate, Davidson Fellows Scholarship, was investigated and found to already be live in ORYN's database (dropped, not duplicated).
